claims.claim: tdTomato was chosen for its photostability and efficient two-photon excitation.
claims.source: To enable cell tracking even when basal Ca2+ levels evoke little GCaMP6f fluorescence, we fused GCaMP6f to the Ca2+-insensitive red fluorescent protein tdTomato, chosen for its photostability and efficient two-photon excitation (Drobizhev et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a paper characterizing tdTomato properties.

claims.claim: A V5 epitope tag was used to link tdTomato to GCaMP6f.
claims.source: A V5 epitope tag (Lobbestael E et al., 2010) served to link tdTomato to GCaMP6f (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This describes the construction of Salsa6f with a citation for the V5 tag.

claims.claim: Salsa6f exhibited a ten-fold dynamic range with brightness comparable to GCaMP6f alone.
claims.source: Salsa6f exhibited a ten-fold dynamic range, with a brightness comparable to GCaMP6f alone (Figure 1A,C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and 1C.

claims.claim: Both components of Salsa6f can be visualized by femtosecond excitation at 900 nm for two-photon microscopy.
claims.source: For two-photon microscopy, both components of Salsa6f can be visualized by femtosecond excitation at 900 nm (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by two-photon imaging data shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: GCaMP6f produces increased green fluorescence during elevations in cytosolic Ca2+, while tdTomato provides stable red fluorescence.
claims.source: GCaMP6f produces increased green fluorescence during elevations in cytosolic Ca2+, while tdTomato provides a stable red fluorescence that facilitates cell tracking and allows for ratiometric Ca2+ imaging (Figure 1D; Video 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data in Figure 1D and Video 1.

claims.claim: Salsa6f is excluded from the nucleus, ensuring accurate measurement of cytosolic Ca2+ fluctuations.
claims.source: Salsa6f is excluded from the nucleus, ensuring accurate measurement of cytosolic Ca2+ fluctuations (Figure 1D,E).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data showing nuclear exclusion in Figures 1D and 1E.

claims.claim: When expressed in human T cells, Salsa6f reported Ca2+ oscillations induced by immobilized αCD3/28 antibodies with high signal to noise ratio and time resolution.
claims.source: When expressed by transfection in human T cells, Salsa6f reported Ca2+ oscillations induced by immobilized αCD3/28 antibodies with a high signal to noise ratio and time resolution (Figure 1E,F).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figures 1E and 1F.

claims.claim: The Salsa6f transgenic cassette was inserted into a Gt(ROSA)26Sor5'-pCAG-FRT-LSL-Salsa6f-WPRE-bGHpA-AttB-FRT-NeoR-AttP-Gt(ROSA)26Sor3' cassette and targeted to the Rosa26 locus in JM8.N4 mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells.
claims.source: Guided by the transgenic targeting strategy for the Ai38 mouse line (Zariwala et al., 2012), we inserted Salsa6f into a Gt(ROSA)26Sor5'-pCAG-FRT-LSL-Salsa6f-WPRE-bGHpA-AttB-FRT-NeoR-AttP-Gt(ROSA)26Sor3' cassette, then targeted it to the Rosa26 locus in JM8.N4 mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This describes the transgenic mouse generation strategy shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Cells positive for the Salsa6f allele were selected by neomycin resistance, and correctly targeted clones were screened by Southern blot.
claims.source: Cells positive for the allele Gt(ROSA)26SorpCAG-FRT-LSL-Salsa6f-WPRE-bGHpA-AttB-FRT-NeoR-AttP were selected by neomycin resistance, and correctly targeted clones were screened by Southern blot (Figure 2B)
claims.evidence: This describes the screening procedure with results shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Chimeric pups carrying the Salsa6f transgene were identified by PCR screening for the Nnt gene.
claims.source: Chimeric pups carrying the Salsa6f transgene were identified by PCR screening for the Nnt gene, as the initial JM8.N4 ES cells were Nnt+/+ while the C57BL/6J blastocysts were Nnt-/- (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This describes the screening strategy with results shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Positive chimeras were bred to R26ΦC31o mice to remove the neomycin resistance gene and produce LSL-Salsa6f F1 founders.
claims.source: Positive chimeras were bred to R26ΦC31o mice to remove the neomycin resistance gene and to produce LSL-Salsa6f F1 founders that are heterozygotic for the Gt(ROSA)26SorpCAG-FRT-LSL-Salsa6f-WPRE-bGHpA-AttB/P allele
claims.evidence: This describes the breeding strategy to generate the final mouse line.

claims.claim: LSL-Salsa6f (Hom) mice were bred to Cd4Cre+/+ mice to obtain reporter mice heterozygous for Salsa6f (Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) mice) that selectively express Salsa6f in T cells.
claims.source: LSL-Salsa6f (Hom) mice were bred to Cd4Cre+/+ mice to obtain reporter mice heterozygous for Salsa6f, designated as Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) mice from here on, that selectively express Salsa6f in T cells (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This describes the breeding strategy shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: 88% of Salsa6f+ cells in thymus were double positive for Cd4 and Cd8.
claims.source: Salsa6f was detected by tdTomato fluorescence on flow cytometry. 88% of these Salsa6f+ cells in thymus were double positive for Cd4 and Cd8 (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: The double-positive stage occurs during T cell development when developing thymocytes express both Cd4 and Cd8 before undergoing positive and negative selection.
claims.source: This is due to the double-positive stage during development, in which developing thymocytes will express both Cd4 and Cd8 before undergoing positive and negative selection to become either mature Cd4+ or Cd8+ T cells.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about T cell development.

claims.claim: Salsa6f was detected in 40% of cells from spleen, 57% from lymph node, and 93% from thymus.
claims.source: Salsa6f was readily detected by the red tdTomato signal in cells from spleen (40%), lymph node (57%), and thymus (93%) (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Double positive cells were not detected in the spleen.
claims.source: As expected, double positive cells were not detected in the spleen (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D and is consistent with T cell development.

claims.claim: More than 98% of Cd4+ and Cd8+ T cells from Cd4-Salsa6f reporter mice were positive for Salsa6f.
claims.source: More than 98% of Cd4+ and Cd8+ T cells from these reporter mice were positive for Salsa6f.
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data.

claims.claim: Salsa6f was detected in 5% of Cd19+ cells and 3% of Cd11b+ cells.
claims.source: Salsa6f was also detected in 5% of Cd19+ cells and 3% of Cd11b+ cells (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: A small fraction of B cells express Cd4 mRNA, which may explain the presence of Salsa6f in Cd19+ cells.
claims.source: A small fraction of B cells express Cd4 mRNA, which may explain the presence of Salsa6f in Cd19+ cells (Zhang and Henderson, 1994).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation and represents a speculative explanation.

claims.claim: Cd11b+ cells positive for Salsa6f may be splenic resident dendritic cells that also express Cd4.
claims.source: Cd11b+ cells positive for Salsa6f may be splenic resident dendritic cells that also express Cd4 (Vremec et al., 2000; Turley et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations and represents a speculative explanation.

claims.claim: The total number and relative frequencies of Cd4+, Cd8+, Cd19+, and Cd11b+ cells were similar between Cd4-Salsa6f mice and Cd4Cre controls.
claims.source: The total number and relative frequencies of Cd4+, Cd8+, Cd19+, and Cd11b+ cells were similar to the Cd4Cre controls (Figure 3F,G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 3F and 3G.

claims.claim: Both heterozygotic and homozygotic Salsa6f-expressing Cd4+ T cells proliferated similar to Cd4Cre controls.
claims.source: Both hetero and homozygotic Salsa6f-expressing Cd4+ T cells proliferated similar to the Cd4Cre controls (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claims.claim: Salsa6f-positive naive Cd4+ T cells from both Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) and Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice readily differentiated into Th1, Th17, and iTreg subtypes similar to Cd4Cre controls.
claims.source: Salsa6f-positive naive Cd4+ T cells from both Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) and Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice readily differentiated into various helper T cell subtypes similar to the Cd4Cre controls (Figure 4C–E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by differentiation assay data shown in Figures 4C-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Adoptively transferred Salsa6f-positive cells readily homed to lymph nodes and exhibited normal motility characteristics.
claims.source: In addition, as described in the companion paper, adoptively transferred Salsa6f-positive cells readily homed to lymph nodes and exhibited normal motility characteristics (Dong et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data in a companion paper.

claims.claim: Salsa6f-expressing T lymphocytes show normal T-cell functions with respect to development, cellular phenotype, cell proliferation, differentiation, homing, and motility.
claims.source: In summary, our results demonstrate normal T-cell functions of Salsa6f-expressing T lymphocytes with respect to development, cellular phenotype, cell proliferation, differentiation, homing, and motility.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Activated Cd4+ T cells expressing Salsa6f exhibited stable red fluorescence and wide fluctuations in green fluorescence due to Ca2+ oscillations resulting from T-cell receptor engagement.
claims.source: Activated Cd4+ T cells expressing Salsa6f exhibited stable red fluorescence and wide fluctuations in green fluorescence due to Ca2+ oscillations resulting from T-cell receptor engagement (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Despite variability in total fluorescence between cells, the basal and peak green/red Salsa6f ratios were comparable between cells and showed up to six-fold increases during peaks in Ca2+ fluctuations.
claims.source: Despite variability in total fluorescence between cells due to individual differences in cell size, the basal and peak green/red Salsa6f ratios (referred from now on as G/R ratio for GCaMP6f/tdTomato intensity) were comparable between cells and showed up to six-fold increases during peaks in Ca2+ fluctuations (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of Salsa6f mouse T cells revealed a 13-fold increase in G/R ratio by ionomycin treatment in Ca2+-free medium followed by Ca2+ addback.
claims.source: Flow cytometric analysis of Salsa6f mouse T cells revealed a 13-fold increase in G/R ratio, by pretreatment with ionomycin in Ca2+-free medium to deplete cytosolic Ca2+ followed by addback of extracellular Ca2+, further emphasizing the high dynamic range of Salsa6f (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: T cells from homozygous Cd4-Salsa6f mice exhibited almost a two-fold increase in tdTomato fluorescence compared to heterozygous mice.
claims.source: T cells from homozygous mice with two allelic copies of the Salsa6f reporter cassette exhibited almost a two-fold increase in tdTomato fluorescence compared to heterozygous mice (Figure 5E), allowing for genetic control of Salsa6f expression level when brightness is an issue.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence measurement data shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: Salsa6f is primarily localized to the cytoplasm and is excluded from the nucleus in naive and activated Cd4+ T cells.
claims.source: Line scans of the confocal images of cells plated on poly-L-lysine-coated coverslips showed that Salsa6f is primarily localized to the cytoplasm and is excluded from the nucleus (Figure 6A,B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal imaging and line scan data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claims.claim: Increasing cytosolic Ca2+ levels using thapsigargin in 2 mM Ca2+ caused a selective increase in the GCaMP6f signal without altering the localization of Salsa6f.
claims.source: Increasing the cytosolic Ca2+ levels using thapsigargin (TG) in 2 mM Ca2+ Ringer's solution caused a selective increase in the GCaMP6f signal, without altering the localization of Salsa6f probe.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data.

claims.claim: Small-molecule dye Ca2+ indicators fluo-4 or fura-2 loaded into Cd4+ T cells are distributed throughout the cell, including the nucleus.
claims.source: In contrast, the small-molecule dye Ca2+ indicators fluo-4 or fura-2 loaded into Cd4+ T cells from Cd4Cre mice are distributed throughout the cell, including the nucleus (Figure 6C and data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: In the PC::G5-tdT transgenic mouse, tdTomato is distributed throughout the cell including the nucleus while GCaMP5G is predominantly in the cytosol.
claims.source: A different transgenic mouse, PC::G5-tdT utilizes an internal ribosomal entry site to express both tdTomato and GCaMP5G as separate proteins that localize differently (Gee et al., 2014), with tdTomato distributed throughout the cell including the nucleus and GCaMP5G predominantly in the cytosol (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and supported by a citation.

claims.claim: In Salsa6f, both red and green fluorescent proteins are co-localized in the cytosol, allowing true ratiometric Ca2+ imaging.
claims.source: In contrast, our tandem probe, Salsa6f, results in both red and green fluorescent proteins co-localized in the cytosol, allowing true ratiometric Ca2+ imaging and facilitating tracking of cells.
claims.evidence: This is a design feature of Salsa6f demonstrated by imaging data.

claims.claim: The GCaMP6f signal increased with increasing Ca2+ concentrations, but the tdTomato signal remained unchanged, suggesting minimal FRET between GCaMP6f and tdTomato.
claims.source: We treated Salsa6f-positive T cells with Ringer's buffer containing Ionomycin and different concentrations of Ca2+ and measured the steady-state GCaMP6f and tdTomato fluorescence signals. The GCaMP6f signal increased as expected with increasing Ca2+ concentrations, but the tdTomato signal remained unchanged (Figure 6D). This suggests that the V5 epitope tag is effective in reducing FRET between GCaMP6f and tdTomato which otherwise may compromise probe performance.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Fura-2 has an in situ Kd of approximately 225 nM at 25°C.
claims.source: We next characterized the in situ Ca2+ affinity of Salsa6f in Cd4+ T cells isolated from Cd4-Salsa6f (Het) mice, using fura-2 as a calibration standard. Fura-2 has an in situ Kd ~225 nM at 25° C (Lewis and Cahalan, 1989)
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a paper characterizing fura-2.

claims.claim: Salsa6f responded with faster rise and decay kinetics than fura-2 to progressive increases in cytosolic Ca2+ levels, especially at lower external Ca2+ concentrations.
claims.source: Salsa6f responded with faster rise and decay kinetics than fura-2 to progressive increases in cytosolic Ca2+ levels, especially at lower external Ca2+ concentrations.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by comparative imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Salsa6f responses saturated at lower cytosolic Ca2+ levels than fura-2 responses.
claims.source: Salsa6f responses also saturated at lower cytosolic Ca2+ levels than fura-2 responses.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by comparative imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators have been reported to have a steeper Hill coefficient than chemical indicators.
claims.source: This is not altogether surprising given that genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators have been reported to have a steeper Hill coefficient than chemical indicators (Badura et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a paper comparing GECIs and chemical indicators.

claims.claim: The estimated in situ Kd for Salsa6f is in the range of 160-300 nM.
claims.source: Assuming that Cd4-Salsa6f T cells reach similar Ca2+ levels as control Cd4Cre cells, we plotted peak and the steady state G/R ratios against the cytosolic Ca2+ concentrations obtained from the fura-2 experiment which yielded an estimated in situ Kd for Salsa6f in the range of 160–300 nM (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: This is derived from calibration experiments shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: Salsa6f is sensitive in detecting cytosolic Ca2+ from 100 nM to 2 μM, which is in the range of physiological cytosolic Ca2+ signals.
claims.source: Based on these results, we conclude that Salsa6f is sensitive in detecting cytosolic Ca2+ from 100 nM - 2 μM, which is in the range of physiological cytosolic Ca2+ signals.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the calibration experiments and known physiological Ca2+ ranges.

claims.claim: TCR engagement activates a canonical Ca2+ signaling pathway in T cells, characterized by IP3-induced Ca2+ release from the endoplasmic reticulum, leading to store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) through Orai1 channels.
claims.source: TCR engagement activates a canonical Ca2+ signaling pathway in T cells, characterized by IP3-induced Ca2+ release from the endoplasmic reticulum, leading to store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) through Orai1 channels (Cahalan and Chandy, 2009; Prakriya and Lewis, 2015).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about T cell Ca2+ signaling supported by citations.

claims.claim: Past studies on T cell Ca2+ signaling have largely relied on indicators like fura-2 and fluo-4 which have the potential drawback of being distributed into the nucleus.
claims.source: Past studies on T cell Ca2+ signaling have largely relied on indicators like fura-2 and fluo-4 which have the potential drawback of being distributed into the nucleus, thus confounding the measurement of pure cytoplasmic Ca2+ signals, a problem particularly notable in T cells with their large nuclear to cytoplasmic volume ratio.
claims.evidence: This is a known limitation of small molecule indicators in T cells.

claims.claim: Salsa6f, with its high dynamic range, ratiometric readout and targeted localization in the cytosol, is well suited to record physiological cytosolic Ca2+ signals.
claims.source: Salsa6f, with its high dynamic range, ratiometric readout and targeted localization in the cytosol, is thus well suited to record physiological cytosolic Ca2+ signals.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the demonstrated properties of Salsa6f.

claims.claim: Depleting ER Ca2+ stores with thapsigargin in Ca2+-free solution produced a small sharp initial peak indicating ER store release followed by a sustained Ca2+ signal upon restoring external Ca2+, indicative of SOCE.
claims.source: To study SOCE more directly, we depleted ER Ca2+ stores in activated and in naïve T cells by applying TG in Ca2+-free solution. We observed a small but sharp initial peak indicating ER store release followed by a sustained Ca2+ signal upon restoring Ca2+ to the external bath, indicative of SOCE (Figure 7A, Video 3 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7A, Video 3, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Almost all cells responded to thapsigargin-induced SOCE.
claims.source: Almost all cells responded to this supra-physiological stimulus (Figure 7A, right panel).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: T cells plated on αCd3/28 showed heterogeneous responses, with some exhibiting asynchronous Ca2+ oscillations of varying frequencies and durations whereas others failed to respond.
claims.source: In contrast, T cells plated on αCd3/28 to activate TCR-induced signaling showed heterogeneous responses, with some exhibiting asynchronous Ca2+ oscillations of varying frequencies and durations whereas others failed to respond (Figure 7B, Video 4).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7B and Video 4.

claims.claim: Ca2+ oscillations in T cells have been attributed to SOCE from repetitive opening and closing of Orai1 channels allowing Ca2+ to enter T cells in a periodic and asynchronous manner.
claims.source: Past studies have attributed these Ca2+ oscillations to SOCE from repetitive opening and closing of Orai1 channels allowing Ca2+ to enter T cells in a periodic and asynchronous manner (Lewis and Cahalan, 1989; Dolmetsch and Lewis, 1994)
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to papers describing Ca2+ oscillations in T cells.

claims.claim: Cells plated on αCd3 alone showed rhythmic oscillatory Ca2+ signals, but the percentage of responding cells was significantly lower than with αCd3/28.
claims.source: Cells plated on αCd3 alone also showed rhythmic oscillatory Ca2+ signals; however, the percentage of responding cells was significantly lower than with αCd3/28, resulting in a lower average signal compared with αCd3/28 stimulation (Figure 7C, Video 5)
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7C and Video 5.

claims.claim: Co-stimulatory signaling through Cd28 enhances the response to TCR activated Ca2+ signals.
claims.source: These results suggest that co-stimulatory signaling through Cd28 enhances the response to TCR activated Ca2+ signals, in alignment with previous observations (Chen and Flies, 2013).
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Perfusion of external solution rapidly past T cells plated on αCd3/28-coated glass coverslips produced a transient rise in cytosolic Ca2+, likely a result of flow shear stress.
claims.source: Finally, we focused on a novel Ca2+ signaling pathway involving mechanosensitive Ca2+-permeable channels. We examined activation of mechanosensitive channels in Salsa6f+ T cells that were plated on αCd3/28-coated glass coverslips, by flowing external solution rapidly past the cells. Perfusion produced a transient rise in the cytosolic Ca2+ signal, likely a result of flow shear stress (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The Piezo family of mechanosensitive channels plays a vital role in cell motility and development.
claims.source: The Piezo family of mechanosensitive channels plays a vital role in cell motility and development (Nourse and Pathak, 2017)
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review on Piezo channels.

claims.claim: It is not known whether Piezo channels are expressed and play a role in immune cell function.
claims.source: but it is not known whether these channels are expressed and play a role in immune cell function.
claims.evidence: This represents a gap in knowledge at the time of the study.

claims.claim: Perfusion of medium including Yoda1, a selective small molecule activator of Piezo1, resulted in robust Ca2+ signals in activated and naive T cells that were larger and more sustained than those activated by perfusion of solvent or media alone.
claims.source: Perfusion of medium including Yoda1, a selective small molecule activator of Piezo1 (Syeda et al., 2015), resulted in robust Ca2+ signals in activated and naive T cells that were larger and more sustained than those activated by perfusion of solvent or media alone (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C, with citation for Yoda1.

claims.claim: Salsa6f detected Ca2+ signals in T cells in response to an activator of Piezo1 channels.
claims.source: In summary, we show Ca2+ signals in T cells in response to an activator of Piezo1 channels.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claims.claim: All subtypes of T cells (naive, Th17, iTregs) responded to plate-bound stimulation of αCd3/28 with oscillatory changes in their cytosolic Ca2+ levels, very similar to the Ca2+ responses in 2-day-activated T cells.
claims.source: All subtypes of T cells responded to plate-bound stimulation of αCd3/28 with oscillatory changes in their cytosolic Ca2+ levels, very similar to the Ca2+ responses in 2-day-activated T cells illustrated in Figure 7B.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data comparing different T cell subsets.

claims.claim: The Ca2+ responses in different T cell subsets were heterogeneous, with some cells showing multiple peaks of varying durations and amplitudes, occasional sustained signals and other cells failing to respond.
claims.source: The responses were heterogeneous, with some cells showing multiple peaks of varying durations and amplitudes, occasional sustained signals and other cells failing to respond.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data from different T cell subsets.

claims.claim: Some individual Th17 cells and iTregs showed higher amplitude Ca2+ signals than any naive T cells, but with a greater percentage of non-responding cells.
claims.source: Whereas the overall average responses were not very different between the three subtypes examined, some individual Th17 cells and iTregs showed higher amplitude signals than any naive T cells, but with a greater percentage of non-responding cells.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data comparing different T cell subsets.

claims.claim: Using two-photon microscopy to image lymph nodes from Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice under steady-state conditions, sporadic localized elevations of green fluorescence indicative of intracellular Ca2+ signaling were observed.
claims.source: Using two-photon microscopy to image lymph nodes from Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) mice under steady-state conditions, we observed sporadic localized elevations of green fluorescence indicative of intracellular Ca2+ signaling (Figure 9A,B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by two-photon imaging data shown in Figures 9A and 9B.

claims.claim: 920 nm is the ideal two-photon excitation wavelength for simultaneous imaging of tdTomato and GCaMP6f as component parts of Salsa6f.
claims.source: Therefore, 920 nm is the ideal two-photon excitation wavelength for simultaneous imaging of tdTomato and GCaMP6f as component parts of Salsa6f.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on optimization experiments shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Some of the green Salsa6f signals were T cell-sized, and the pattern of red Salsa6f fluorescence is consistent with the exclusion of the Salsa6f indicator from the nucleus.
claims.source: Some of the green Salsa6f signals were T cell-sized, and the pattern of red Salsa6f fluorescence observed is consistent with the exclusion of the Salsa6f indicator from the nucleus (Figure 9C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figure 9C.

claims.claim: Numerous bright, transient green fluorescent signals termed 'sparkles' were observed, which were much smaller in area (about 2 µm2).
claims.source: In addition, we observed numerous bright, transient green fluorescent signals which were much smaller in area (about 2 µm2 in area) (Figure 9B,D; Video 6). We term these fluorescent transients 'sparkles', because during rapid playback of time-lapse image streams cells appear to sparkle.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figures 9B, 9D, and Video 6.

claims.claim: An image processing approach was developed to minimize fluctuations in background fluorescence and sensitively identify cell-wide Ca2+ signals and sparkles.
claims.source: Because T cells move rapidly and are not uniformly distributed in lymph nodes, we developed an image processing approach in order to minimize fluctuations in background fluorescence and in order to sensitively identify cell-wide Ca2+ signals and sparkles (Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This describes the image processing methodology shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Based on the one-to-one correspondence of tdTomato and GCaMP6f, fluctuations in green fluorescence due to cell movement and distribution were estimated and subtracted out.
claims.source: Based on the one-to-one correspondence of tdTomato and GCaMP6f, we estimated and subtracted out fluctuations in green fluorescence due to cell movement and distribution.
claims.evidence: This describes the image processing approach.

claims.claim: After processing, sparkles were found to occur widely across the imaging field.
claims.source: After processing, sparkles were found to occur widely across the imaging field (Figure 9E–G)
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by processed imaging data shown in Figures 9E-G.

claims.claim: Many sparkles reached a characteristic maximum intensity.
claims.source: and many reached a characteristic maximum intensity (compare Figure 9F and G).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by imaging data shown in Figures 9F and 9G.

claims.claim: Hundreds of sparkle events with a mean amplitude of 6.5 SD above background were observed in each 25 min imaging session.
claims.source: Hundreds of events with a mean amplitude of 6.5 SD above background were observed in each 25 min imaging session (one image stack every five seconds), whereas fewer than one event exceeding our threshold was expected to occur from random noise fluctuations.
claims.evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of imaging data.

claims.claim: Sparkles were more frequent than cell-wide transients.
claims.source: Sparkles were more frequent than cell-wide transients (Figure 9H)
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by quantification shown in Figure 9H.

claims.claim: Sparkles extended over a median area of 1.9 µm2.
claims.source: extended over a median area of 1.9 µm2 (n = 441 sparkles from three lymph nodes; Figure 9I)
claims.evidence: This is based on quantification of sparkle areas shown in Figure 9I.

claims.claim: Sparkles usually lasted for only one or two consecutive frames.
claims.source: and usually lasted for only one or two consecutive frames (Figure 9J).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by temporal analysis shown in Figure 9J.

claims.claim: Sparkle trace shape differs from that expected for autofluorescent cell processes drifting into the imaging field.
claims.source: Sparkle trace shape differs from that expected for autofluorescent cell processes drifting into the imaging field (Figure 9K).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by comparison shown in Figure 9K.

claims.claim: Sparkles correspond to local Ca2+ signals restricted to small subcellular domains of T cells migrating through the lymph node.
claims.source: Taken together, these observations suggest that sparkles correspond to local Ca2+ signals restricted to small subcellular domains of T cells migrating through the lymph node.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the characteristics of sparkles observed in the imaging data.

claims.claim: Small green fluorescence transients seen in lymph nodes after adoptive transfer were similar in intensity to transients seen in Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) lymph nodes.
claims.source: Small green fluorescence transients seen in lymph nodes after adoptive transfer were similar in intensity to transients seen in Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) lymph nodes (Figure 10A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by comparison of imaging data shown in Figure 10A.

claims.claim: Small, bright, and brief green fluorescence signals traced back to their origin were found in red fluorescent Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) T cells.
claims.source: When small, bright, and brief green fluorescence signals were traced back, they were found to originate in red fluorescent Cd4-Salsa6f (Hom) T cells (Figure 10B–M).

results.result: Salsa6f, a novel ratiometric genetically encoded Ca2+ indicator, was created by fusing GCaMP6f to tdTomato via a V5 epitope linker. The probe exhibits a ten-fold dynamic range, brightness comparable to GCaMP6f alone, nuclear exclusion, and can be excited at 900 nm for two-photon microscopy. When expressed in human T cells, Salsa6f reported Ca2+ oscillations with high signal-to-noise ratio.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C44 collectively demonstrate the successful design and in vitro characterization of Salsa6f. The experimental data in Figures 1A-F show the probe's dynamic range, brightness, two-photon excitability, nuclear exclusion, and ability to report Ca2+ oscillations in human T cells. The design rationale (selection of GCaMP6f and tdTomato, use of V5 linker) is clearly described and validated.

results.result: A transgenic mouse line was generated with Salsa6f targeted to the Rosa26 locus for Cre-dependent expression. LSL-Salsa6f mice were crossed with Cd4Cre mice to produce Cd4-Salsa6f mice that selectively express Salsa6f in T cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C49 describe the transgenic mouse generation strategy with supporting data in Figure 2. The targeting strategy, ES cell screening by Southern blot, chimera identification by PCR, and breeding scheme are all documented with experimental evidence. This establishes the successful generation of the Cd4-Salsa6f mouse line.

results.result: In Cd4-Salsa6f mice, 88% of Salsa6f+ cells in thymus were double positive for Cd4 and Cd8, consistent with T cell development. Salsa6f was detected in 40% of spleen cells, 57% of lymph node cells, and 93% of thymus cells. More than 98% of Cd4+ and Cd8+ T cells were Salsa6f+, with small percentages in Cd19+ (5%) and Cd11b+ (3%) cells. Cell populations were similar to Cd4Cre controls.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C58 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3. The expression pattern is consistent with Cd4-driven Cre expression during T cell development. The presence of Salsa6f in small percentages of B cells and dendritic cells is acknowledged with speculative explanations supported by citations (C56-C57). Normal cell populations compared to controls support that the transgene does not perturb immune cell development.

results.result: T cell development and function were unaffected in Cd4-Salsa6f mice. Both heterozygous and homozygous Salsa6f-expressing Cd4+ T cells proliferated normally and differentiated into Th1, Th17, and iTreg subtypes similar to controls. Adoptively transferred Salsa6f+ cells homed normally to lymph nodes with normal motility.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C62 are supported by proliferation and differentiation data in Figure 4, with additional motility data referenced from a companion paper (C61). The comprehensive assessment of T cell function (proliferation, differentiation, homing, motility) demonstrates that Salsa6f expression does not perturb T cell biology, which is critical for validating the mouse model.

results.result: Activated Cd4+ T cells from Cd4-Salsa6f mice exhibited stable red fluorescence and wide fluctuations in green fluorescence due to Ca2+ oscillations. The G/R ratio showed up to six-fold increases during Ca2+ peaks and a 13-fold increase with ionomycin treatment. Homozygous mice showed two-fold higher tdTomato fluorescence than heterozygous mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C66 are supported by imaging and flow cytometry data in Figure 5. The ratiometric measurements demonstrate the functional utility of Salsa6f for Ca2+ imaging in T cells. The dose-dependent expression in heterozygous vs. homozygous mice provides flexibility for experimental design.

results.result: Salsa6f is localized to the cytoplasm and excluded from the nucleus in naive and activated Cd4+ T cells. This contrasts with small-molecule indicators (fluo-4, fura-2) and the PC::G5-tdT mouse, where indicators are distributed throughout the cell including the nucleus. In Salsa6f, both fluorescent proteins are co-localized in the cytosol, enabling true ratiometric Ca2+ imaging.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C71 are supported by confocal imaging data in Figure 6A-C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1. The line scan analysis clearly demonstrates cytoplasmic localization and nuclear exclusion. The comparison with other indicators highlights a key advantage of Salsa6f for measuring pure cytosolic Ca2+ signals.

results.result: The GCaMP6f signal increased with increasing Ca2+ concentrations while tdTomato signal remained unchanged, suggesting minimal FRET between GCaMP6f and tdTomato due to the V5 epitope linker.
results.evaluation: Claim C72 is supported by experimental data in Figure 6D showing that tdTomato fluorescence does not change with Ca2+ concentration. This validates the design choice of using the V5 linker to minimize FRET, which would otherwise compromise the ratiometric measurements.

results.result: The in situ Kd of Salsa6f in Cd4+ T cells was estimated to be 160-300 nM using fura-2 (Kd ~225 nM) as a calibration standard. Salsa6f responded with faster kinetics than fura-2 and saturated at lower Ca2+ levels, consistent with GECIs having steeper Hill coefficients than chemical indicators. Salsa6f is sensitive to detecting cytosolic Ca2+ from 100 nM to 2 μM.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C78 are supported by calibration experiments in Figure 6E-G. The methodology of using fura-2 as a standard is appropriate, and the estimated Kd range is consistent with the in vitro Kd of GCaMP6f. The conclusion that Salsa6f is sensitive in the physiological Ca2+ range is well-supported. However, the calibration assumes that Cd4-Salsa6f T cells reach similar Ca2+ levels as control cells (C77), which is a reasonable but unverified assumption.

results.result: Salsa6f was used to study store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) in T cells. Depleting ER Ca2+ stores with thapsigargin in Ca2+-free solution produced a small initial peak (ER release) followed by sustained Ca2+ signal upon Ca2+ restoration (SOCE). Almost all cells responded to this stimulus.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C83 are supported by imaging data in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A. The biphasic response (initial peak followed by sustained elevation) is characteristic of SOCE. Claims C79-C81 provide appropriate context about T cell Ca2+ signaling and the advantages of Salsa6f for these measurements.

results.result: T cells plated on αCd3/28 showed heterogeneous Ca2+ oscillations, with some cells exhibiting asynchronous oscillations and others failing to respond. Cells on αCd3 alone showed lower response rates than αCd3/28, suggesting that co-stimulation through Cd28 enhances TCR-activated Ca2+ signals.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C87 are supported by imaging data in Figure 7B-C. The heterogeneous responses and the difference between αCd3 and αCd3/28 stimulation are clearly demonstrated. The interpretation that Cd28 co-stimulation enhances responses is supported by a citation (C87) and is consistent with established T cell biology.

results.result: Perfusion of external solution produced transient Ca2+ rises in T cells, likely due to flow shear stress. Perfusion with Yoda1, a Piezo1 activator, resulted in robust Ca2+ signals that were larger and more sustained than perfusion alone. This represents the first observation of Piezo1-mediated Ca2+ signals in T cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C92 are supported by imaging data in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B-C. The Yoda1 responses are clearly larger than control perfusion, supporting Piezo1 activation. However, the claim that this is the first observation in T cells (C92) should be interpreted cautiously as it depends on the literature at the time of publication. The study does not directly demonstrate Piezo1 expression or use Piezo1 knockout controls, so the mechanism remains somewhat inferential.

results.result: All T cell subtypes (naive, Th17, iTregs) responded to αCd3/28 with oscillatory Ca2+ signals similar to activated T cells. Responses were heterogeneous, with some Th17 cells and iTregs showing higher amplitude signals than naive T cells, but with more non-responding cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C95 are supported by imaging data in Figure 8. The comparison across T cell subsets demonstrates the utility of Salsa6f for studying Ca2+ signaling in different T cell populations. The heterogeneity and differences between subsets are clearly documented.

results.result: Two-photon imaging of Cd4-Salsa6f lymph nodes revealed sporadic Ca2+ signals including cell-wide transients and numerous small (~2 μm²), brief 'sparkles'. An image processing approach was developed to subtract background fluorescence based on the tdTomato signal. Hundreds of sparkles (mean 6.5 SD above background) were detected per imaging session, occurring more frequently than cell-wide transients. Sparkles lasted 1-2 frames and correspond to local Ca2+ signals in subcellular domains of migrating T cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C109 are supported by two-photon imaging data in Figure 9 and supplementary figures. The image processing approach is well-described and validated. The statistical analysis showing hundreds of events above a stringent threshold (5.4 SD) with mean amplitude of 6.5 SD is convincing. The characteristics of sparkles (size, duration, frequency) are quantified. The interpretation that sparkles represent local subcellular Ca2+ signals (C109) is a reasonable inference based on their properties, though the exact mechanism is not determined.

results.result: In adoptively transferred Cd4-Salsa6f T cells, sparkles were traced to red fluorescent T cells and localized to the front or back of motile cells. Ratiometric imaging confirmed significant differences in Ca2+ concentration between front and back (p<0.0001). Motile T cells exhibit Ca2+ signals restricted to cytoplasmic subregions.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C115 are supported by imaging data in Figure 10. The adoptive transfer approach allows visualization of individual cells, and the ratiometric analysis clearly demonstrates subcellular Ca2+ gradients. The statistical analysis (Mann-Whitney test, p<0.0001) is appropriate and convincing. This demonstrates the utility of Salsa6f for mapping subcellular Ca2+ signals in vivo.

results.result: Salsa6f preserves the performance of GCaMP6f with similar dynamic range, superior to FRET-based GECIs. The Ca2+ affinity (160-300 nM) is well-suited for detecting cellular Ca2+ signals. Inclusion of tdTomato enables ratiometric imaging and measurement of Ca2+ concentrations. Salsa6f is uniformly distributed in the cytosol with nuclear exclusion.
results.evaluation: Claims C116-C120 summarize the key properties of Salsa6f demonstrated throughout the manuscript. These are supported by the experimental data in Figures 1, 5, and 6. The comparisons to other indicators are supported by citations and experimental data.

results.result: No effects of Salsa6f expression were found in Cd4+ immune cells, even in homozygous mice, with respect to cellular phenotype, proliferation, differentiation, homing, and motility.
results.evaluation: Claim C122 is supported by experimental data in Figures 3-4 and a companion paper. The comprehensive assessment of T cell function demonstrates that Salsa6f does not perturb cell biology, addressing the concern raised in C121. This is critical for validating the mouse model for physiological studies.

results.result: Salsa6f was used to detect Ca2+ influx from SOCE, TCR stimulation, and Piezo1 activation. Differences in Ca2+ signaling patterns were detected between naive T cells, Th17 cells, and iTregs.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C124 summarize the applications of Salsa6f demonstrated in Figures 7-8. These results showcase the versatility of the probe for studying different Ca2+ signaling pathways and T cell subsets.

results.result: The red fluorescence of Salsa6f enables cell identification and tracking in complex tissues. Both tdTomato and GCaMP6f are excited at 920 nm for two-photon imaging, enabling visualization hundreds of micrometers deep. Salsa6f enables ratiometric imaging in intact lymph nodes and measurement of absolute Ca2+ concentrations.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C134 describe the advantages of Salsa6f for in vivo imaging, supported by two-photon imaging data in Figures 9-10 and Figure 9—figure supplement 1. The ability to image deep into lymph nodes, track cells, and perform ratiometric measurements in vivo represents a significant advance.

results.result: The Salsa6f transgenic mouse enables detection of rare Ca2+ signaling events. The one-to-one correspondence of tdTomato and GCaMP6f allows subtraction of resting fluorescence, improving background uniformity. This approach, combined with uniform cytosolic labeling, enabled detection of sparkles and mapping of local Ca2+ signals to subcellular regions.
results.evaluation: Claims C135-C144 describe the advantages of the Salsa6f mouse for detecting rare events, supported by the sparkle detection in Figures 9-10. The image processing approach is well-validated. Claim C144 is speculative about future capabilities but is a reasonable extrapolation. The comparison to previous Ca2+ probes (C137-C139) is supported by citations and highlights the advantages of Salsa6f.

results.result: Small molecule Ca2+ indicators like fura-2 and fluo-4 have expanded understanding of Ca2+ signaling but have limitations: they cannot be targeted to specific compartments or cell populations, are unsuitable for long-term studies due to leakage, and do not faithfully report pure cytosolic Ca2+ due to nuclear diffusion.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C12 describe well-established properties and limitations of small molecule Ca2+ indicators, supported by citations (C9) and general knowledge in the field. These claims provide appropriate context for the development of Salsa6f.

results.result: GECIs were first developed as FRET-based probes with advantages including genetic targeting, local Ca2+ measurement, and long-term expression. Initial GECIs had poor performance, but successive improvements led to high-performing variants like GCaMP6 and GECO families. The latest GECIs match or exceed small-molecule indicators in performance and enable diverse applications including optogenetics and single-channel recording.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C25 provide a comprehensive review of GECI development, supported by numerous citations to the relevant literature. This background appropriately contextualizes the development of Salsa6f and establishes the rationale for choosing GCaMP6f as the Ca2+-sensitive component.

results.result: Previous GECI transgenic mice used older variants or had limitations. The Ai38 mouse uses GCaMP3 with Cre/lox for selective expression, avoiding side effects of global expression. The PC::G5-tdT mouse has improved functionality but GCaMP5G and tdTomato localize differently and tdTomato expression is variable. Single fluorescent protein-based indicators are problematic for imaging motile cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C34 review previous transgenic GECI mice, supported by citations. These claims establish the rationale for developing Salsa6f as an improvement over existing approaches, particularly for imaging motile cells. The limitations of PC::G5-tdT (C32-C33) are based on known properties of IRES-based expression.
